rationale.conceptual: The method is a standard Metropolis Monte Carlo simulation of the spin-1/2 Ising model on a simple cubic lattice with periodic/free boundary conditions. While the film geometry and oscillating field add minor complexity, the core algorithm is textbook and widely used. No novel derivation or custom method is required.
rationale.execution: The task involves two straightforward steps: running the Monte Carlo simulation for multiple parameter combinations and extracting critical temperatures from specific heat maxima. The pipeline is a single Python script using NumPy, with simple file I/O. No multi-stage orchestration, no external tooling, just sequential parameter sweeps.

difficulty.reasoning: Standard Monte Carlo simulation of an Ising model thin film with oscillating field. Method is textbook, no novel algorithms. Pipeline is a single script with parameter sweep, simple I/O. CPU-bound computation with large number of spin updates but negligible memory and no external data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The Monte Carlo simulation requires many spin updates (1.6e12) across 66 parameter combinations, driving CPU time but not GPU acceleration. Memory is low (few MB for lattice, energy arrays). No external dataset is used; all configuration is generated on the fly.
